failed_activities.error_message: Failure occurred while updating etl_watermark_control. Transaction rolled back due to dead-letter socket timeout. 1,420 delta records landed in bronze/patients/2026/09/24/ but control table last_watermark remains at 2026-09-23T00:00:00. Next scheduled run will cause duplicate primary key collisions in Silver.

ai_diagnosis.technical_root_cause: The ingestion activity wrote 1,420 delta files/records into the Bronze partition (bronze/patients/2026/09/24/) but failed to commit the etl_watermark_control update due to a dead-letter socket timeout while updating the control table; the transaction rolled back leaving control.last_watermark at 2026-09-23T00:00:00Z while Bronze contains records up to 2026-09-24T18:30:00Z. This creates a state desynchronization: the storage layer advanced but the control-state did not, so a subsequent scheduled run that uses the control table to determine the next delta will attempt to reprocess the same records and may produce duplicate-primary-key collisions in Silver. No telemetry indicates any exfiltration of PII; the issue is data-state integrity (watermark drift) caused by a control-table write failure (socket timeout) during commit.

ai_decision.rationale: Advance the etl_watermark_control idempotently to the actual max timestamp observed in Bronze only after verifying the expected delta files/counts. The conditional (WHERE last_watermark = previous_value) update is idempotent and atomic: it will only move the watermark if the control table is still at the pre-failure value, avoiding data-loss or skipping data. This prevents a re-run from duplicating records while preserving all landed Bronze files.

WHERE table_name = 'patients' AND last_watermark = TIMESTAMP '2026-09-23T00:00:00Z';

Next scheduled run will cause duplicate primary key collisions in Silver.

ai_diagnosis.technical_root_cause: The bronze ingestion wrote 1,420 delta records to the bronze path (bronze/patients/2026/09/24/) with a max event timestamp of 2026-09-24T18:30:00Z, but the etl_watermark_control update failed and was rolled back due to a dead-letter socket timeout on the control DB transaction. As a result the control table still reports last_watermark = 2026-09-23T00:00:00Z. This desynchronization will cause the next scheduled ingestion/transform to reprocess the same delta and produce duplicate primary-key collisions in Silver. There is no evidence from telemetry of data exfiltration or PII leakage; the primary risk is data integrity and downstream processing failures.

ai_decision.rationale: Idempotently advancing the control-table watermark to match the already-landed bronze files is the safest immediate corrective action: it prevents duplicate re-processing of the same bronze delta on the next run and allows downstream Silver processing to continue deterministically. The update uses a conditional WHERE (current watermark value) to avoid clobbering any concurrent legitimate changes. Actions include recording an audit entry and then triggering the downstream Silver transform to process the landed delta once the control state is consistent.

failed_activities.error_message: Cannot find the table 'FakeTableNonExistent_12345' because it does not exist or you do not have permission.

ai_diagnosis.technical_root_cause: The Lookup activity LKP_Simulate_Fail failed with a SQL_ERROR because the referenced table 'FakeTableNonExistent_12345' cannot be found or is inaccessible. This is most commonly caused by: (a) the table was never created or was dropped/renamed, (b) the activity is pointing at the wrong database/schema, or (c) the service principal/identity used by the pipeline lacks SELECT permission on the table. There is no evidence in the telemetry of a data exfiltration or HIPAA/PII leak; this is an availability/metadata/permission failure preventing the pipeline from reading a lookup table.

ai_decision.rationale: Automatic creation of a stub table or blind retry risks silent data corruption or propagation of incomplete reference data. The safest idempotent action is to halt further dependent processing, record an auditable incident, perform non-destructive checks to confirm the missing object and permissions, and require human remediation before rerunning. This preserves patient-data integrity and HIPAA compliance while enabling a deterministic re-run once the underlying issue is fixed.
